answer: An agent proves a distinct physical presence by reporting signed wind vectors from a station downwind of a wildfire ember plume, cross-checked against two neighbouring stations that must see the same plume direction. The tide of smoke is anchored to public fire-perimeter maps, and each wind signal is sealed with a hardware key whose cipher cannot be copied, so a Sybil operator would need many real stations around many fires, and a copied report fails when neighbouring vectors point elsewhere.
